# core/wgnoise.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/wgnoise.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The Noise_IKpsk2_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s pattern,
as a set of pure functions on byte strings (no clocks, no random numbers,
no sockets): the caller brings the keys, the ephemeral private keys, the
sender indexes and the TAI64N timestamp, so every message can be checked
against a reference.

The handshake state is 64 bytes, the chaining key C then the hash H, and
is changed in place. A message goes through four steps:

  initiator: wgn_initiation        -> 116 bytes (add the two MACs with wgn_macs)
  responder: wgn_consume_initiation   (who sent it, when; the state follows)
  responder: wgn_response          -> 60 bytes, and the transport keys
  initiator: wgn_consume_response     -> the transport keys

A transport key pair is 64 bytes: the key this side sends with, then the
key it receives with. A Diffie-Hellman result of all zeros (a low-order
public key) refuses the message, as in the reference implementation.

Not here: replay windows, timers, the choice of when to ask for a cookie and the
data messages: those belong to the caller.

`import "core/wgnoise.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/blake2s.bastio](core-blake2s.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/chacha20poly1305.bastio](core-chacha20poly1305.md), [core/x25519.bastio](core-x25519.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`wgn_public`](#wgn_public) | The public key of the private key `priv`. |
| [`wgn_initiation`](#wgn_initiation) | The initiator's first message (116 bytes, without the MACs). |
| [`wgn_consume_initiation`](#wgn_consume_initiation) | The responder reads an initiation (the first 116 bytes of the message; the MACs are the caller's to check). |
| [`wgn_response`](#wgn_response) | The responder's answer (60 bytes, without the MACs) to an initiation whose state is st (after wgn_consume_initiation). |
| [`wgn_consume_response`](#wgn_consume_response) | The initiator reads the response (60 bytes; MACs and the receiver index are the caller's to check) to the initiation whose state is st. |
| [`wgn_macs`](#wgn_macs) | body || mac1 || mac2 for a handshake message addressed to the holder of static public key `rpub`. |
| [`wgn_mac1_ok`](#wgn_mac1_ok) | Do the last 32 bytes of `msg` hold a mac1 made for the holder of static public key `mypub`? (A message shorter than 32 bytes does not.) |
| [`wgn_mac2_ok`](#wgn_mac2_ok) | Does `msg` carry a mac2 made with `cookie` (16 bytes)? |
| [`wgn_cookie`](#wgn_cookie) | The 16-byte cookie for the peer at `who` (the bytes of its address and port, at most 32) under the 32-byte `secret`. |
| [`wgn_cookie_reply`](#wgn_cookie_reply) | The cookie reply (64 bytes) for the initiation with sender index `ridx` and mac1 `mac1` (16 bytes), from the holder of static public key `mypub`. |
| [`wgn_consume_cookie_reply`](#wgn_consume_cookie_reply) | The cookie in the cookie reply `msg` (64 bytes) to our initiation whose mac1 was `mac1`, from the holder of static public key `rpub`; `None` if the reply is not type 3, or was not sealed by that holder for that mac1. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `wgn_public`

```bastio
fn wgn_public(priv: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(priv) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The public key of the private key `priv`: X25519 of the base point.

### `wgn_initiation`

```bastio
fn wgn_initiation(spriv: &Bytes, spub: &Bytes, rpub: &Bytes, epriv: &Bytes, idx: u64, tai: &Bytes, st: &mut Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(spriv) == 32 && blen(spub) == 32 && blen(rpub) == 32 && blen(epriv) == 32 && idx < 4294967296 && blen(tai) == 12 && blen(st) == 64
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && (result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 116)
```

The initiator's first message (116 bytes, without the MACs): sender index
`idx`, ephemeral private key `epriv`, static keys spriv/spub, the
responder's static public key rpub and the 12-byte TAI64N `tai`. st
becomes the state after it. None if a Diffie-Hellman result is all zeros.

Example:

```bastio
let mut spriv = balloc(32);
bset(&mut spriv, 0, 8);    // the low three bits are cleared by X25519
let mut rpriv = balloc(32);
bset(&mut rpriv, 0, 16);    // the low three bits are cleared by X25519
let mut epriv = balloc(32);
bset(&mut epriv, 0, 24);    // the low three bits are cleared by X25519
let mut erpriv = balloc(32);
bset(&mut erpriv, 0, 32);    // the low three bits are cleared by X25519
let psk = balloc(32);
let spub = wgn_public(spriv);
let rpub = wgn_public(rpriv);
let epub = wgn_public(epriv);
let tai = balloc(12);
let mut st_i = balloc(64);
let mut st_r = balloc(64);
let mut keys_i = balloc(64);
let mut keys_r = balloc(64);
let mut bad = 1;
match wgn_initiation(spriv, spub, rpub, epriv, 7, tai, &mut st_i) {
  Option::None => {},
  Option::Some(init) => {
    let none = balloc(0);
    let full = wgn_macs(init, rpub, none);
    let cookie = balloc(16);
    let fullc = wgn_macs(init, rpub, cookie);
    if wgn_mac1_ok(full, rpub) && !wgn_mac1_ok(full, spub) && wgn_mac2_ok(fullc, cookie) && !wgn_mac2_ok(full, cookie) {
      match wgn_consume_initiation(rpriv, rpub, init, &mut st_r) {
        Option::None => {},
        Option::Some(who) => {
          match wgn_response(&mut st_r, erpriv, epub, spub, psk, 9, 7, &mut keys_r) {
            Option::None => {},
            Option::Some(resp) => {
              if wgn_consume_response(&mut st_i, epriv, spriv, psk, resp, &mut keys_i) {
                // What one side sends with, the other receives with.
                let a = bytes_slice(keys_i, 0, 32);
                let b = bytes_slice(keys_r, 32, 64);
                if bytes_eq(a, b) { bad = 0; }
                bfree(a);
                bfree(b);
              }
              bfree(resp);
            },
          }
          bfree(who);
        },
      }
    }
    bfree(fullc);
    bfree(cookie);
    bfree(full);
    bfree(none);
    bfree(init);
  },
}
bfree(keys_r);
bfree(keys_i);
bfree(st_r);
bfree(st_i);
bfree(tai);
bfree(epub);
bfree(rpub);
bfree(spub);
bfree(psk);
bfree(erpriv);
bfree(epriv);
bfree(rpriv);
bfree(spriv);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `wgn_consume_initiation`

```bastio
fn wgn_consume_initiation(rpriv: &Bytes, rpub: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes, st: &mut Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(rpriv) == 32 && blen(rpub) == 32 && blen(msg) == 116 && blen(st) == 64
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && (result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 76)
```

The responder reads an initiation (the first 116 bytes of the message; the
MACs are the caller's to check): None if it is not one, or its static
field or timestamp does not open, or a Diffie-Hellman result is zero;
otherwise the initiator's static public key (32 bytes), its TAI64N (12)
and its ephemeral public key (32). The caller looks the static key up
among its peers and compares the timestamp with the last one it took.

### `wgn_response`

```bastio
fn wgn_response(st: &mut Bytes, epriv: &Bytes, ei_pub: &Bytes, si_pub: &Bytes, psk: &Bytes, idx: u64, ridx: u64, keys: &mut Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(epriv) == 32 && blen(ei_pub) == 32 && blen(si_pub) == 32 && blen(psk) == 32 && idx < 4294967296 && ridx < 4294967296 && blen(keys) == 64
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && blen(keys) == 64 && (result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 60)
```

The responder's answer (60 bytes, without the MACs) to an initiation whose
state is st (after wgn_consume_initiation): sender index `idx`, the
initiator's index `ridx`, the responder's ephemeral private key `epriv`,
the initiator's ephemeral and static public keys and the pre-shared key
(32 zero bytes for none). Also gives the responder's transport keys:
keys := send || receive. None for a zero Diffie-Hellman result.

### `wgn_consume_response`

```bastio
fn wgn_consume_response(st: &mut Bytes, epriv: &Bytes, spriv: &Bytes, psk: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes, keys: &mut Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(epriv) == 32 && blen(spriv) == 32 && blen(psk) == 32 && blen(msg) == 60 && blen(keys) == 64
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && blen(keys) == 64
```

The initiator reads the response (60 bytes; MACs and the receiver index
are the caller's to check) to the initiation whose state is st: with its
own ephemeral private key and static private key and the pre-shared key.
True if it opens; keys := the initiator's send || receive keys.

### `wgn_macs`

```bastio
fn wgn_macs(body: &Bytes, rpub: &Bytes, cookie: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(body) <= 1024 && blen(rpub) == 32 && (blen(cookie) == 0 || blen(cookie) == 16)
  ensures blen(result) == blen(body) + 32
```

body || mac1 || mac2 for a handshake message addressed to the holder of
static public key `rpub`: mac1 = MAC(HASH("mac1----" || rpub), body) (a
keyed BLAKE2s with 16 output bytes); mac2 is MAC(cookie, body || mac1)
when `cookie` is 16 bytes, and zeros when it is empty.

### `wgn_mac1_ok`

```bastio
fn wgn_mac1_ok(msg: &Bytes, mypub: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(msg) <= 1056 && blen(mypub) == 32
```

Do the last 32 bytes of `msg` hold a mac1 made for the holder of static
public key `mypub`? (A message shorter than 32 bytes does not.)

### `wgn_mac2_ok`

```bastio
fn wgn_mac2_ok(msg: &Bytes, cookie: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(msg) <= 1056 && blen(cookie) == 16
```

Does `msg` carry a mac2 made with `cookie` (16 bytes)?

### `wgn_cookie`

```bastio
fn wgn_cookie(secret: &Bytes, who: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32 && blen(who) <= 32
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

The 16-byte cookie for the peer at `who` (the bytes of its address and
port, at most 32) under the 32-byte `secret`.

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let who = bfrom("abcdef");
let c = wgn_cookie(secret, who);
let n = blen(c);
bfree(c);
bfree(who);
bfree(secret);
if n != 16 { return 1; }
```

### `wgn_cookie_reply`

```bastio
fn wgn_cookie_reply(mypub: &Bytes, ridx: u64, nonce: &Bytes, cookie: &Bytes, mac1: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(mypub) == 32 && ridx < 4294967296 && blen(nonce) == 24 && blen(cookie) == 16 && blen(mac1) == 16
  ensures blen(result) == 64
```

The cookie reply (64 bytes) for the initiation with sender index `ridx`
and mac1 `mac1` (16 bytes), from the holder of static public key `mypub`:
the 16-byte `cookie` sealed under the 24-byte `nonce`, which must be
random and used once.

Example:

```bastio
let mypub = balloc(32);
let nonce = balloc(24);
let cookie = balloc(16);
let mac1 = balloc(16);
let msg = wgn_cookie_reply(mypub, 5, nonce, cookie, mac1);
let mut ok = blen(msg) == 64 && bget(msg, 0) == 3 && bget(msg, 4) == 5;
match wgn_consume_cookie_reply(msg, mypub, mac1) {
  Option::Some(c) => { ok = ok && bytes_eq(c, cookie); bfree(c); },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
bfree(msg);
bfree(mac1);
bfree(cookie);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(mypub);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `wgn_consume_cookie_reply`

```bastio
fn wgn_consume_cookie_reply(msg: &Bytes, rpub: &Bytes, mac1: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(msg) == 64 && blen(rpub) == 32 && blen(mac1) == 16
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 16
```

The cookie in the cookie reply `msg` (64 bytes) to our initiation whose
mac1 was `mac1`, from the holder of static public key `rpub`; `None` if
the reply is not type 3, or was not sealed by that holder for that mac1.

Example:

```bastio
let rpub = balloc(32);
let nonce = balloc(24);
let cookie = bfrom("0123456789abcdef");
let mut mac1 = balloc(16);
let msg = wgn_cookie_reply(rpub, 1, nonce, cookie, mac1);
bset(&mut mac1, 0, 1);                       // another initiation's mac1
let mut refused = true;
match wgn_consume_cookie_reply(msg, rpub, mac1) {
  Option::Some(c) => { refused = false; bfree(c); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(msg);
bfree(mac1);
bfree(cookie);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(rpub);
if !refused { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `wgn_hash`

```bastio
fn wgn_hash(a: &Bytes, b: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(a) + blen(b) <= 1048576
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: HASH(a || b): BLAKE2s-256.

### `wgn_kdf_step`

```bastio
fn wgn_kdf_step(t0: &Bytes, prev: &Bytes, i: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(t0) == 32 && blen(prev) <= 32 && i < 256
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: One HMAC step of the KDF: HMAC(t0, prev || i).

### `wgn_kdf`

```bastio
fn wgn_kdf(key: &Bytes, input: &Bytes, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(key) == 32 && blen(input) <= 1024 && n >= 1 && n <= 3
  ensures blen(result) == 32 * n
```

Internal: The first n (1 to 3) outputs of WireGuard's KDF(key, input), 32 bytes each.

### `wgn_seal`

```bastio
fn wgn_seal(k: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, plain: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(k) == 32 && blen(plain) < 1048576
  ensures blen(result) == blen(plain) + 16
```

Internal: ChaCha20-Poly1305 with the counter-0 nonce (4 zero bytes, then 8).

### `wgn_open`

```bastio
fn wgn_open(k: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, sealed: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(k) == 32 && blen(sealed) < 1048576
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) + 16 == blen(sealed)
```

Internal: see the module comment.

### `wgn_dh`

```bastio
fn wgn_dh(priv: &Bytes, p: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(priv) == 32 && blen(p) == 32
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32
```

Internal: DH(priv, pub), or None when the result is all zeros.

### `wgn_start`

```bastio
fn wgn_start(st: &mut Bytes, rpub: &Bytes)
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(rpub) == 32
  ensures blen(st) == 64
```

Internal: st := HASH(C0 || identifier) chain up to the responder's static key:
C = HASH(construction), H = HASH(HASH(C || identifier) || rpub).

### `wgn_mix_hash`

```bastio
fn wgn_mix_hash(st: &mut Bytes, data: &Bytes)
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(data) <= 4096
  ensures blen(st) == 64
```

Internal: H := HASH(H || data).

### `wgn_mix_key1`

```bastio
fn wgn_mix_key1(st: &mut Bytes, input: &Bytes)
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(input) <= 1024
  ensures blen(st) == 64
```

Internal: C := KDF1(C, input).

### `wgn_mix_key2`

```bastio
fn wgn_mix_key2(st: &mut Bytes, input: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(input) <= 1024
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: (C, k) := KDF2(C, input): the key k.

### `wgn_dh_key2`

```bastio
fn wgn_dh_key2(st: &mut Bytes, priv: &Bytes, p: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(priv) == 32 && blen(p) == 32
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && (result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32)
```

Internal: DH(priv, p) mixed into C with KDF2: the key, or None for a zero result.

### `wgn_dh_key1`

```bastio
fn wgn_dh_key1(st: &mut Bytes, priv: &Bytes, p: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(priv) == 32 && blen(p) == 32
  ensures blen(st) == 64
```

Internal: DH(priv, p) mixed into C with KDF1: false for a zero result.

### `wgn_h`

```bastio
fn wgn_h(st: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(st) == 64
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: H as its own 32 bytes (the associated data of the next sealed field).

### `wgn_keys`

```bastio
fn wgn_keys(st: &Bytes, first_is_send: bool) -> Bytes
  requires blen(st) == 64
  ensures blen(result) == 64
```

Internal: The transport keys from C: KDF2(C, empty), the initiator's sending key
first, as `first_is_send` says for this side.

### `wgn_mix_response`

```bastio
fn wgn_mix_response(st: &mut Bytes, epriv: &Bytes, epub_peer: &Bytes, dh2_priv: &Bytes, dh2_pub: &Bytes, psk: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(st) == 64 && blen(epriv) == 32 && blen(epub_peer) == 32 && blen(dh2_priv) == 32 && blen(dh2_pub) == 32 && blen(psk) == 32
  ensures blen(st) == 64 && (result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 32)
```

Internal: Mixes the response's shared secrets into st after the ephemeral key er
is in: DH(e, ei) and DH(e, si) with KDF1, then psk with KDF3 (its middle
output into H); returns the key that seals the empty field, or None for a
zero Diffie-Hellman result. `epriv`/`epub_peer` and `spriv`/`spub_peer`
name which side's keys are used (the responder uses its ephemeral private
key with the initiator's keys; the initiator the other way round).

### `wgn_cookie_key`

```bastio
fn wgn_cookie_key(pub: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(pub) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Internal: HASH("cookie--" || pub), the key cookie replies to the holder of
static public key `pub` are sealed with.
